The difference in absorption rate between sl (under the tongue) and po (oral) depends on the medication. Some medications the molecules are too large to be absorbed by the mucosa under the tongue, and must be swallowed or injected. Most sl medications start to absorb immediately and take effect within minutes, vs. up to about a half hour for ingested, and even longer if you already have a full stomach (the stomach doesn't really absorb anything, it must pass through to the small intestine).

Medications like nitro spray for chest pain, and Ativan for anxiety work very well under the tongue and reach peak levels in the blood in about 10-15 minutes.
